name: plugin-source-example
description: Reference plugin example - contributing operations through a source plugin

askturret.coreDependencyIsWildcard: "*" is deliberate, not laziness. npm links a workspace package only while its version SATISFIES the declared range, so a pin converts a stable local link into one that silently expires. Measured: with a non-satisfying range npm abandons the link and requests @askturret/mcp-core from registry.npmjs.org, where nothing is published (the project is pre-1.0 and has released nothing) — and `^0.1.0` would stop matching at the very next minor, since 0.2.0 does not satisfy it under semver's 0.x caret rule. These examples are EXECUTED by CI ('Plugin examples run'), so that would break the build, not merely the demo. "*" always matches, so the example always runs against current source, which is the whole point of shipping it in-tree. IF YOU COPY THIS EXAMPLE into a real project, replace "*" with a real range: outside this workspace it accepts any future major.
askturret.testsNotRequired: Runnable demo, not a library. Unlike its exporter sibling it DOES own its plugin, because a source plugin is adopter code by definition and there is no shipped reference source to load. That would normally be the rot risk plugin-otel-exporter warns about, so this example is executed by CI (test-integrity, 'Plugin examples run') rather than merely built: it compiles its operations through the real compiler, so a broken plugin seam fails the build instead of printing something plausible.
